name: io.pandex/law
title: Pandex
description: Official legislation and case law for AI agents, every past version with dates. Read-only.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find passages of legislation and court decisions. Answers with the passages themselves (an article, a paragraph of a judgment), each with its document, date, id and url. A query that names a text ("art. 6:162 BW", "§ 823 BGB", "ECLI:NL:HR:2019:2006", "32016R0679 art 17") is answered with that text first. Write the query in the language of the documents; set jurisdiction when you know it.

cites.description: Only passages that cite this document or article: an id, id#element, or a citation.

court.description: Words from the court's name, e.g. "Hoge Raad", "Bundesgerichtshof", "Grand Chamber".

doc_type.description: A document type as shown in results, e.g. regulation, directive, act, judgment, opinion.

facets.description: Also count the passages that hold every word by jurisdiction, source and year.

jurisdiction.description: One or more of: at, be, br, ca (with its parts, each also asked alone: ca-bc, ca-on), ch (with its parts, each also asked alone: ch-ag, ch-ar, ch-bl, ch-bs, ch-ge, ch-gl, ch-gr, ch-ju, ch-lu, ch-ne, ch-nw, ch-sg, ch-sh, ch-so, ch-sz, ch-tg, ch-ti, ch-ur, ch-vd, ch-zg, ch-zh), coe, cw, cz, de, dj, dk, es, eu, fi, fr, gb, it, lu, mt, mx, ng, nl, pl, pt, se, tn, us (with its parts, each also asked alone: us-co). Comma-separated.

kind.description: Only laws, only court decisions, or only treaties.

lang.description: Two-letter language to match and answer in (texts that exist in several languages). Default: the query's language.

max_tokens.description: Size of the answer in tokens, 200–8000. Default 1500.

mode.description: hybrid (default): words and meaning (decisions: both together; laws: meaning when no passage holds every word); text: only words; meaning: only meaning.

offset.description: Results to skip, for the next page: the answer says the offset of the next one.

query.description: Words, a question, or a citation. Put a phrase in double quotes to require it literally.

sort.description: relevance (default); date: newest first; date_asc: oldest first; cited: most cited first. The last three order the passages that hold every word.

within.description: Only passages of this document: an id or a citation.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read a document or one part of it in its official wording: a whole short text, one article (element), everything under a chapter, or the text as it stood on a date. One article of a law comes with the leading decisions on it: those cited most by the decisions that cite the article. Long documents come in pieces; the answer says how to continue.

at.description: Read the text in force on this day, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current text.

cases.description: With one article of a law: the leading decisions on it. Default true.

element.description: The part to read: an element id from a result or outline (art_6:162, art_823, chp_2) or its number as written ("6:162", "823", "Annex III", "recital 26").

from.description: Continue reading from this element id (given by a previous answer).

history.description: With element: also list the periods of every version of it.

id.description: An id from a result, or an identifier or citation: an ECLI, a CELEX number, "BGB", "art. 6:162 BW".

lang.description: Two-letter language, for texts that exist in several.

max_tokens.description: Size of the answer in tokens, 200–8000. Default 1500.

tools.name: get_outline
tools.description: The structure of a document: its parts, chapters and articles with their headings and element ids. Use it to find the right article of a long law before reading it.

at.description: The structure as it stood on this day, YYYY-MM-DD.

id.description: An id from a result, or an identifier or citation.

lang.description: Two-letter language, for texts that exist in several.

max_tokens.description: Size of the answer in tokens, 200–8000. Default 1500.

under.description: Only the structure below this element (a part or chapter).

tools.name: get_citations
tools.description: What cites a document or one of its articles (direction "in": the leading ones first, those the other citing documents cite most, each with the passage that cites it), or what it cites (direction "out"), with the places where. Targets we do not hold are listed as written. To search inside the citing passages, use search with cites.

direction.description: in (default): documents that cite it. out: what it cites.

element.description: Only citations of, or from, this element.

id.description: An id from a result, or an identifier or citation.

max_tokens.description: Size of the answer in tokens, 200–8000. Default 1500.

order.description: For direction in. leading (default): those the other citing documents cite most. newest: by date.

relation.description: Only one relation: cites, amends, repeals, implements, consolidates, appeals, joins.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: What changed in a law, or in the laws of a source or country: the articles whose wording changed, was inserted or repealed, newest first, with the day. A wording not yet in force is listed too. One law by its id gives all the changes held; a source or a jurisdiction goes five years back.

id.description: One law: an id from a result, or an identifier or citation.

jurisdiction.description: Or the laws of one jurisdiction ("ch").

lang.description: Two-letter language, for texts that exist in several.

offset.description: Lines to skip, for the next page.

since.description: Only changes from this day on, YYYY-MM-DD.

source.description: Or the laws of one source id from list_sources.

until.description: Only changes up to this day, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: The sources that are loaded, per jurisdiction: what each one holds, its languages, how many documents and as of which day. With a jurisdiction: also its institutions (courts, legislators), what is held of each and what is not.
